title: Finite support of higher direct images
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-morphism-conventions, def-pc-scheme]. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ [pqf-def-coherent], (1) each $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ is quasi-coherent. If $S$ is quasi-compact, there is an integer $n=n(X,S,f)$ such that (2) $R^pf_*\mathcal{F}=0$ for every $p\ge n$ and every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{F}$, and (3) for every morphism $g:S'\to S$ of schemes, with $X'=S'\times_S X$ [def-pc-fibre-product], projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$, and every quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-module $\mathcal{F}'$, one has $R^p f'_*\mathcal{F}'=0$ for every $p\ge n$.

proof.text: To prove (1), restrict the derived direct image to an affine open $V\subseteq S$ using [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. On the affine base $S$, apply [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] to the property that every $R^if_*\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal G$ on a quasi-compact open. On an affine open $U$, [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] gives the assertion in degree zero and the cited cohomology-presheaf statement together with [lem-pc-affine-vanishing] gives vanishing in positive degrees. For $U\cup V$ (with $U$ quasi-compact, $V$ affine, $a,b,c,g$ the restrictions of $f$ to $U,V,U\cap V,U\cup V$ and $\mathcal G$ quasi-coherent on $U\cup V$), apply [lem-sc-mayer-vietoris-open-cover] to the cover of $g^{-1}(T)$ by $a^{-1}(T)$ and $b^{-1}(T)$ for every open $T\subseteq S$; by its naturality in inclusions of open covers these long exact sequences form a long exact sequence of presheaves of $\mathcal O_S$-modules $T\mapsto H^p(g^{-1}(T),\mathcal G)$, etc. Sheafification is exact [lem-weil-pbc-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] and by [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf] it turns these presheaves into $R^pg_*\mathcal G$, $R^pa_*(\mathcal G|_U)\oplus R^pb_*(\mathcal G|_V)$, $R^pc_*(\mathcal G|_{U\cap V})$, giving the relative Mayer--Vietoris long exact sequence, which expresses each cohomology sheaf as an extension of kernels and cokernels of maps between the corresponding quasi-coherent sheaves; kernels and cokernels are checked on affine opens, and [lem-pc-quasi-coherent-extension] gives quasi-coherence of the extensions. This proves (1) locally on $S$ and hence globally.

proof.text: For the uniform bound, when $S$ is affine define $P(U)$ for a quasi-compact open $U\subseteq X$ to mean: there is an integer $n_U$ such that for every affine $S'\to S$ and every quasi-coherent module $\mathcal G$ on $S'\times_S U$, one has $H^p(S'\times_S U,\mathcal G)=0$ for all $p\ge n_U$. If $U$ is affine, then every $S'\times_S U$ is affine, so [lem-pc-affine-vanishing] gives $n_U=1$. If $U$ is quasi-compact and $V$ is affine, then $(U\cup V)'=U'\cup V'$ and $(U\cap V)'=U'\cap V'$; applying [lem-sc-mayer-vietoris-open-cover] to the base-changed cover and the induction bounds gives the gluing property with bound one larger than the maximum. Thus [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] gives $P(X)$.

For a quasi-compact base $S$, choose a finite affine cover $S=\bigcup_j S_j$ and apply Step 2 to each restricted morphism over $S_j$; let $n$ be the maximum of the finitely many bounds. For any base change $S'\to S$, cover $S'$ by affine opens contained in the inverse images of the $S_j$. Each such affine open maps to one affine $S_j$, so Step 2 gives vanishing in degrees $p\ge n$ for every quasi-coherent module on its inverse image. These opens form a basis, and hence the same $n$ works for every $S'\to S$.

source.place: Lemma 30.4.5, Tag 01XJ, quasi-compact-base and arbitrary-base-change conclusion

proof.text: Fix a point $y\in S'$. The affine open neighborhoods $V\subseteq S'$ of $y$ contained in some $g^{-1}(S_j)$ are cofinal among all open neighborhoods of $y$ (Step 3). For such $V$, $f'^{-1}(V)=V\times_SX=V\times_{S_j}f^{-1}(S_j)$, so Step 2 for $f^{-1}(S_j)\to S_j$ with the affine base change $V\to S_j$ gives $H^p(f'^{-1}(V),\mathcal F'|_{f'^{-1}(V)})=0$ for $p\ge n$. Hence the filtered colimit of these groups over this cofinal system is zero. The stalk isomorphism in [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf] identifies this colimit with $(R^pf'_*\mathcal F')_y$, so every stalk vanishes and therefore $R^pf'_*\mathcal F'=0$.

tool_uses.why: The qcqs finite-affine-cover induction principle supplies the open-union induction used to obtain a finite cohomological bound.
Restriction of derived direct image to an open base is needed for affine-locality.
Affine morphisms provide the degree-zero quasi-coherence and higher vanishing base case.
The higher direct image is identified with the cohomology presheaf on affine opens.
The relative Mayer--Vietoris long exact sequence supplies the gluing step.
Extensions of quasi-coherent sheaves remain quasi-coherent in the gluing step.
Exactness of sheafification turns the Mayer--Vietoris sequences of presheaves into the relative sequence of higher direct images (added by reviewer R-fsh3127).
Vanishing of higher cohomology of quasi-coherent modules on affine schemes, base case of both inductions (declared by reviewer R-fsh3127).
